risks: Timeout, quota, or malformed JSON without attempt ceilings, cooldowns, and closed-schema/inode checks can loop or be stored as success; a changed output inode or stale byte overwrite is a classified failure, not completion.

Missing Lean pins, occupied GPU, disk or memory pressure, and a dead owner must not be labeled proof failures or used to kill unrelated jobs; a planned backlog item is not a dead worker and must not enter a restart loop.
A spawned PID, heartbeat file, green fixture, or model text can be mistaken for campaign activation or a verified shorter proof when owner, guardian, or fresh native receipts are absent.
actions: Probe only owned fixtures for provider timeout/quota, malformed JSON, changed output inode, missing native environment, occupied GPU, disk pressure, and dead owner; retry bounded transient transport after PID and ownership checks, then record the reason and cooldown.

When a capability is blocked, resume only eligible disjoint CPU or Grok work; keep planned tasks inactive until reviewed producer argv, a protected native validator, and resource/input receipts exist; do not stop unrelated processes or shared caches.

Treat supervisor progress as observable only with a live owned lock, guardian and heartbeat evidence, and one strict grok-4.7 llm_router receipt; stop at the task budget and keep failed evidence without inventing success.
acceptance_boundaries: Proposal only: this review does not run fault probes, start the supervisor, or complete JLR-033/034. Actual tests and Lean compilation are separate evidence and are not claimed here.

Quota, disk, GPU, missing-pin, and ownership failures remain infrastructure statuses. They are not proof failures, token improvements, or official-score gains. Theorem and computation semantics stay unchanged and out of scope.
The 23 planned tasks stay non-selectable until activation receipts exist. Startup acceptance needs task progress plus a real router call, not a PID, this review file, or a green fixture suite alone.
